body:
I didn't realize NetworkInterface methods take such long time. Let me try to fix it asap.

Global uniqueness is another problem to think about though.

Do you have a clue in what environment they are seeing the blocking calls?  I took a look into the JDK source code for the reported native methods and what they do are just opening a socket and doing some ioctl to get the flags.

Env info specified in the http://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/IDEA-122367:
Platform: OS X 10.9 (mavericks)
Hardware: Macbook Pro late 2013, i5 2.4Ghz, 256gb SSD, 16gb RAM
JRE: 1.7.0_51-b13 x86_64

I asked my colleague to provide more details.

I had the issue under the latest JDK 1.7 on Windows 7 x64 machine with Virtual Box, VMWare virtual machine network adapters. I also had VPN interface and working network interface. No VM were running that time. The issue could have been caused by DNS resolve or probably some pings

I have a QEMU Win 7 x86 machine with JDK 1.7u51, but couldn't reproduce the problem:
- with/without an OpenVPN adapter
- with/without a bridged network adapter
- with/without a reachable DNS server
- with/without Windows firewall

The possible workaround in the IntelliJ would be to set the system property programmatically before `DefaultChannelId` is loaded so that a user doesn't have to specify the machine ID system property.

Yes, we use this workaround. 

But please note — netty 5 was used for 4 months before IDEA 13.1 release, and only one internal user reported about this bug (all EAP users, IDEA team and related teams haven't experienced this issue). But IDEA widely used in different environments, so, after release we got a lot of disappointed users.

My point — such unreliable methods should not be performed without control. Such behaviour could be unexpected for Netty library users, so, by default, more simplified and reliable logic should be used. It is not convenient to share knowledge "never use netty 5 without set magic properties".

I think, @jonnyzzz can provide you remote connection or something like it if you want to understand whats going on.

@develar I agree that those methods are unreliable for an unknown reason, but they are not really supposed to be unreliable.  `io.netty.util.NetUtil` also invokes `NetworkInterface.isLoopback()`, but we didn't get a report about that class yet, which is weird.  I want to make sure what is causing this problem.

On the other hand, I also would like to explore an alternative ways to generate better channel ID which is unlikely to collide.  Any suggestion would be appreciated.
- `UUID.randomUUID()` uses `SecureRandom` internally, so it will block easily once it runs out of entrophy.  I can just use Netty's `ThreadLocalRandom` which uses a secure random integer as a seed, though.
- I could set some time limit for `defaultMachineId()` but I guess it's not what you really want.
@jonnyzzz Let me try VirtualBox and VMware Player first.  Meanwhile, could you please paste the output of `ipconfig /all` for both VMs?

I meant I was not running the code _inside_ a VM. I only mentioned I had so much hypervisors installed on the machine.

Ah, I see.  I can try that.  Thanks for the info.  It will take some time though because I don't have a Windows machine set up for developments.
If @normanmaurer has one, he could try too. ;-)

It seems like this is related with `-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true` option.  In Windows with VirtualBox and VMware Player installed, I see `defaultMachineId()` takes about 2.5 seconds when `-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true` is specified.  If unspecified, it takes less than 400ms.  `NetworkInterface` reportes the machine has 20 NICs and most of them are virtual interfaces.

So, getting NIC information in some platform is a time-consuming operation, and we should avoid iterating over all NICs.
